<context query="context reads choose between Lore's own stores and Utopia backend" template="default" budget="8000">
<section name="Conventions" source="repo" priority="1">
<document source="specs/utopia-graph-mirror/spec.md" type="spec" relevance="1.00" tokens="187">
## Reads choose a backend

The side-by-side experiment of the ADR-052 amendment of 2026-10-16: every ingest writes to both stores, and each context read names the store it reads, `lore`, `utopia` or `both`, per request or through the repo's `settings.context_backend`, with Lore the default. A source Utopia cannot read yet answers `<source>: no Utopia reader yet`; Lore's data is never served under Utopia's name. The switch is specified where it lives: [context assembly](../context-assembly/spec.md) FR-1.5 to FR-1.8, [`GET /api/context`](../api-routes/context/spec.md), [`lore_search_context`](../mcp-tools/search-context/spec.md), [`lore_search_memory`](../mcp-tools/search-memory/spec.md) and [context evals](../context-evals/spec.md) FR4.4.
</document>
<document source="docs/building-lore/context-store-comparison.md" type="doc" relevance="0.94" tokens="261">
## Why we measured

Lore keeps its knowledge in its own stores: a Dgraph trace graph, pgvector chunks and a memory schema. Since ADR-052 it also mirrors each repository's specs, ADRs, test runs and code links into a Utopia knowledge base. The plan is not to move by decree. Every ingest writes to both stores, every read can name the store it reads from (`backend: lore | utopia | both`), and a store is switched to Utopia only once the context evals show Utopia answering at least as well for that kind of data, two weeks running.

This is the first run of that measurement. The Utopia side is young: it has one reader so far, and Utopia knowledge bases exist for only seven of the twelve onboarded repositories.

# Which store answers context questions best

**For people deciding where Lore's knowledge should live.** This records the side-by-side comparisons of Lore's own stores and Utopia as the source of the context an agent gets: the first, run on 2026-10-16, and the re-runs of 2026-10-19 (below), and what they say about the switch.
</document>
</section>
<section name="Architecture Decisions" source="adrs" priority="2">
<document source="adrs/ADR-052-code-to-spec-graph-mirrored-in-utopia.md" type="adr" relevance="1.00" tokens="355">
## Amendment 2026-10-16: reads choose a backend

Before any read moves to Utopia, Lore and Utopia run side by side, so that what each returns for the same question can be compared:

- **Every ingest writes to both.** The spec and ADR mirror above is the first; each other source follows as its Utopia writer lands. Lore's stores stay the default answer.
- **A read names its backend: `lore`, `utopia` or `both`** (`KnowledgeBackend`, `libs/shared/src/domain/knowledge-backend.ts`). `GET /api/context`, `GET /api/search-context`, the `search` action of `POST /api/memory`, `POST /api/context-evals` and the MCP tools `lore_assemble_context`, `lore_search_context` and `lore_search_memory` take an optional `backend`; context assembly falls back to the repo's `settings.context_backend`, then to `lore`. An unknown backend is a 400.
- **No silent fallback.** A source with no Utopia reader answers `<source>: no Utopia reader yet` in Utopia's place, never Lore's data under Utopia's name; a search tool the MCP adapter would answer offline refuses `utopia` and `both` rather than read Lore's stores. `both` puts Lore's assembly first and Utopia's second, each section labelled with its store and each on half the token budget.
- **No source has a Utopia reader yet.** They land one source at a time behind this switch; the context evals grade one backend per call, and scoring `both` side by side is a following change.
</document>
</section>
<section name="Agent Memory" source="memories" priority="2">
<document source="session:re-cinq/lore" type="episode" tokens="141">
**session:re-cinq/lore** (episode) [observed]: FR4.4 allows callers to post { backend: "lore" } or { backend: "utopia" } to POST /api/context-evals to get verdicts from a single store.

**session:re-cinq/lore** (episode) [observed]: Calling assembleContext with backend: 'utopia' returns a context block where every active template section renders '<source>: no Utopia reader yet' without querying Lore's stores.

**session:re-cinq/lore** (episode) [observed]: The --backend parameter for context-evals accepts values of lore, utopia, or both with a default value.
</document>
</section>
</context>
